_purpose: Names lie; contents do not. Each shape is a whole tree as it would exist on disk under a qBittorrent completed directory. A classifier that reads only the torrent name will get several of these wrong.
_note: Sizes are in bytes and are load-bearing: several tie-breaks below are only decidable by size or duration, not by extension.

shapes.label: clean movie release
shapes.why: the sample must be excluded and the subtitle carried; a largest-file heuristic gets this right, an alphabetical-first heuristic gets it wrong

shapes.label: season pack, flat
shapes.why: ONE torrent produces THIRTEEN destination paths. Any data model with a 1:1 torrent-to-destination mapping cannot represent this.

shapes.label: complete series, nested season dirs
shapes.why: an existing season directory must be re-derived, not copied verbatim ('Season 1' -> 'Season 01' for Jellyfin's zero-padding recommendation)

shapes.label: album with multi-disc subfolders and artwork
shapes.why: Navidrome groups on ALBUM+ALBUMARTIST tags, so the move must not rewrite tags; cover.jpg is one of the folder-image names Navidrome looks for and must travel with the album

shapes.label: manga series as archives
shapes.why: Komga makes a Series from the parent folder and a Book from each file — this shape maps 1:1 and must be preserved, not flattened

shapes.label: manga as loose page images

expect.reason: Komga indexes CBZ/CBR/EPUB/PDF only; loose images are invisible to it

shapes.why: filing this into a Komga library produces an empty-looking library and the user blames Orphanarr; refusing with an explanation is the correct behaviour

shapes.label: multi-disc PS1 game
shapes.why: RomM models a multi-file game as a folder under the platform slug; splitting the discs into separate top-level entries produces three broken games

shapes.label: single-file audiobook
shapes.why: .m4b is the one extension that is near-decisive for audiobook; without it, a folder of mp3s is indistinguishable from an album by extension alone

shapes.label: audiobook that looks exactly like an album
shapes.why: THE decisive music-vs-audiobook signal is track duration (~50 min/track, 38 tracks) and mono/low bitrate — NOT the file extension, NOT the folder name. If the design has no duration probe it must say so and route this to manual review.

shapes.label: album that looks exactly like an audiobook
shapes.why: one 61-minute track; the duration heuristic from shp-009 misfires here. Any duration rule needs a stated failure mode, and this is it.

shapes.label: torrent containing two unrelated media types
shapes.why: no single destination is correct; a byte-majority rule silently discards the album and the book

shapes.label: already-organised library dropped in as one torrent
shapes.why: the torrent root is a library root, not a release. Treating it as one movie produces '/Movies/Movies (unknown)/'.

shapes.label: hardlink idempotency
shapes.note: destination already contains a file with the SAME st_ino as the source
shapes.why: a second scan pass must recognise its own previous work; otherwise every poll interval duplicates or errors

shapes.label: RAR-packed release

expect.reason: archived; extraction is Unpackerr's job, not Orphanarr's

shapes.why: moving the rar set into a Plex library produces an unplayable folder; declaring extraction out of scope must be an explicit non-goal, not an oversight
